blocks.content: Jharkhand's polity chapter follows the standard Indian state structure (Governor, CM, bicameral-free Assembly) but features a few distinctive elements — notably its high tribal-reservation profile and the unusual political volatility of its first 13 years, both worth knowing in detail.

cells: Unicameral — Jharkhand Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha), 81 elected seats + provision for nominated representation of the Anglo-Indian community historically (subsequently discontinued nationally after the 104th Amendment, 2019)
28 seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes, 9 for Scheduled Castes out of 81 — reflecting Jharkhand's very high tribal population share (Chapter 8)
Santosh Kumar Gangwar, in office since 31 July 2024
Hemant Soren (Jharkhand Mukti Morcha), in office (current stint) since 4 July 2024

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Jharkhand's Assembly reservation profile — 28 ST + 9 SC seats out of 81 total — is one of the highest tribal-reservation proportions of any Indian state Assembly, directly reflecting the state's demographic profile (Chapter 8) and shaping its electoral/political dynamics significantly.
Political Volatility & the Chief Ministerial Sequence

Jharkhand experienced marked political instability in its first 13 years as a state (2000-2013), with frequent changes of government, several spells of President's Rule, and Chief Ministers who at various points governed without holding an Assembly seat at the time of appointment (a constitutionally permitted but practically precarious arrangement, requiring the CM to secure Assembly membership within six months) — Shibu Soren notably was sworn in as CM without being an MLA on more than one occasion, including a 2005 ministry that collapsed within roughly a fortnight.

Political stability improved somewhat from the mid-2010s, with Raghubar Das (BJP) serving a full five-year term from 2014 to 2019 — the first Chief Minister in Jharkhand's history to do so — followed by Hemant Soren (JMM) leading a JMM-Congress-RJD coalition government from December 2019.

Hemant Soren's tenure has itself seen significant recent turbulence: he stepped down in January 2024 amid a legal case (linked to a land-related matter) shortly before arrest, was succeeded briefly by fellow JMM leader Champai Soren (February-July 2024), and then returned as Chief Minister on 4 July 2024 after developments in the legal proceedings, before leading the JMM-led alliance to victory in the subsequent Assembly election and continuing in office into 2025-26.

cells: 2014-2019 — first CM to complete a full 5-year term

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Raghubar Das (2014-2019) was Jharkhand's FIRST Chief Minister to complete a full five-year term — a frequently tested fact reflecting the state's notably volatile political history in its earlier years (2000-2013), during which no ministry survived a full assembly cycle.

items: 81-seat unicameral Assembly: 28 ST-reserved + 9 SC-reserved seats — among the highest tribal-reservation proportions of any Indian state.
Current (2026) Governor: Santosh Kumar Gangwar (since 31 July 2024); current CM: Hemant Soren (JMM, current stint since 4 July 2024).
14 Lok Sabha seats; 6 Rajya Sabha seats; Jharkhand High Court at Ranchi.
Jharkhand saw marked political instability 2000-2013 (frequent President's Rule, short-lived ministries); Raghubar Das (2014-19) was the first CM to complete a full term.
Hemant Soren has served multiple non-continuous stints as CM, including a 2024 resignation/arrest, brief succession by Champai Soren, and his own return to office in July 2024.
